methodological_rigor.justification: Multicohort phase II trial (TAPISTRY) with prospective design. PD-L1 inhibitor-naive patients with TMB-high (≥13 and ≥16 mut/Mb) advanced/metastatic solid tumors received atezolizumab. Primary endpoint: IRC-assessed ORR at TMB≥16 mut/Mb. Secondary endpoints specified (ORR, DOR, PFS, safety at TMB≥13). Includes pediatric cohort (15 mg/kg dosing). Standard trial design with IRC assessment and survival monitoring.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: TMB-high tumors identified across solid malignancies as biomarker for anti-PD-L1 response. TAPISTRY evaluates atezolizumab across TMB-high cohorts, informing precision immunotherapy selection. Directly applicable to patient stratification and treatment decisions across tumor types.

reporting_quality.justification: Phase II trial with clearly specified primary/secondary endpoints, IRC assessment, and safety monitoring. Cohort definitions (TMB≥13 vs ≥16) explicitly stated. Missing: detailed baseline characteristics table (in abstract only), CONSORT checklist completeness, potential missing data handling, subgroup analysis pre-specification.

novelty_literature.justification: TMB as biomarker for anti-PD-L1 efficacy well-established. TAPISTRY applies existing TMB threshold to atezolizumab in multicohort design. Contributes evidence for TMB-high selection across tumor types but lacks mechanistic innovation or threshold optimization.

writing_presentation.justification: Trial design clearly presented. Primary/secondary endpoints explicitly specified. TMB cutoff options (≥13, ≥16) transparently described. Pediatric inclusion appropriately noted. Standard trial reporting format.

key_strengths: Prospective multicohort phase II design evaluating atezolizumab in TMB-high populations across solid tumors
IRC assessment of primary endpoint (ORR) providing independent efficacy determination
Evaluation of two TMB cutoffs (≥13 and ≥16 mut/Mb) to address inconsistent thresholds in literature
Inclusion of pediatric patients expanding applicability beyond adult oncology
key_concerns: Limited novelty: TMB-high selection established; trial confirms rather than advances precision medicine
Single-arm design without control group limits comparative efficacy assessment
Tumor heterogeneity across multicohort approach may confound results; subgroup-specific responses not distinguished in abstract
TMB measurement methodology, cutoff derivation, and lab validation not detailed in abstract
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-designed prospective trial with clear endpoints and broad applicability. Tier 3 based on confirmatory rather than novel design.
